card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning when the index contains no legacy file-offset entries. When a queried transaction resides in a block that was pruned after being indexed, RPC and REST lookups return candidate block hashes so users can retrieve the block on demand using getblockfrompeer. Pruned nodes can also initialize a partial txindex from their earliest available block, reporting its start height in getindexinfo. This eliminates a long-standing incompatibility that prevented storage-limited nodes from indexing transactions.
evidence: PR description: "After #35531, each txindex entry now points to the block hash containing the tx instead of the file location of the block... This PR enables maintaining a txindex while pruned. If a txid lookup tries to read a tx from a pruned block from after the index was started, the hash of the missing block is surfaced to the caller."
Diff in init.cpp removes the unconditional init check: 'Prune mode is incompatible with -txindex.'
problem: -txindex and -prune have historically been mutually exclusive because txindex entries referenced absolute block file offsets that became invalid upon pruning. Users running storage-constrained pruned nodes could not index or look up confirmed transactions without keeping hundreds of gigabytes of raw block history on disk.

risk.why: Bugs in index synchronization or lookup logic could return false block associations or crash RPC and REST endpoints when querying pruned or partially indexed chains.

scope_notes: Refactors BaseIndex prune handling by replacing the AllowPrune() boolean with an IndexPrunePolicy enum. Extends JSONRPCError to accept an optional structured error data payload for pruned block hash reporting.
summary: Allows running txindex concurrently with block pruning on databases that do not contain legacy block-file-offset entries. When a transaction lookup targets a pruned block, GetTransaction, RPC, and REST endpoints surface candidate block hashes so callers can fetch the block on demand via getblockfrompeer. Pruned nodes can also initialize a partial index from their oldest retained block, tracking and reporting the starting height in getindexinfo.
